correctness.rationale: The proof separates \(\mathbb R^n=\operatorname{Range}(H)\oplus\ker H\). The constraint depends only on the range component. A nonzero objective component in \(\ker H\) therefore gives an explicit feasible ray with value tending to \(-\infty\). When \(b\in\operatorname{Range}(H)\), both constraint and objective factor through the range quotient, where \(H\) is positive definite and the source theorem applies exactly. Embedding the quotient inverse gives \(H^\dagger\), and arbitrary nullspace additions give all strict-case minimizers. The dual equation \(H^{1/2}u=b\) is solvable exactly under the same range condition; its minimum-norm solution has squared norm \(b^{\mathsf T}H^\dagger b\).

value.rationale: Rank-deficient ellipsoids and cylinders are standard uncertainty geometries, so the extension is not an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem identifies a sharp compatibility test \(b\in\operatorname{Range}(H)\) that separates immediate unboundedness from the usual attainment boundary. It also shows that a naive inverse-to-pseudoinverse substitution misses two structural effects: a new nullspace escape mechanism and loss of strict-case uniqueness. The result gives a complete solvability certificate and optimizer description that can be checked from the range, pseudoinverse, and one scalar \(\beta\).
